summary: Parkevtate Vosianc reviews CoreWeave (CRWV) after quarterly results that lifted the stock 26% the next day, asking whether it is still a buying opportunity after his upgrade about six weeks ago and conviction raise on 5 November. Revenue reached $3.7 billion, up 168% year over year and above guidance, adding $1 billion from the prior quarter, while adjusted operating income hit $379 million versus $230 million forecast and the newest contracts are among the most profitable ever underwritten. Backlog grew to approximately $133 billion and active power more than doubled since the start of the year to over 1.7 gigawatts, with data centres online faster than expected — unlike IREN, whose build-out slipped by a couple of months. He spends much of the video on funding, the industry's central worry: data centres need huge upfront cash before revenue arrives, a mismatch he compares to building an apartment block before collecting rent. Management says funding is anchored by secured lending, customer prepayments and operating cash flow, not the circular-financing scheme some fear. The risk is real — over $50 billion of long-term debt and revenue that only materialises if the capacity gets built — but the stock trades at a forward price-to-sales ratio of 1.283, near its cheapest in years, and his fair value is $94 against a $61.53 price. Call: CRWV BUY at $61.53, fair value $94, reiterated, but only for high-risk-tolerance investors, with Nvidia as a key strategic supporter ahead of its 17 November earnings.
